entries.title: Esther 3:1
segments: Haman; supposed to have been an Amalekite, and a descendant of one of their ancient kings.
Despots not unfrequently advance to places of honor and power the most wicked of their subjects.

entries.title: Esther 3:2
segments: Bowed not; it was not contrary to the laws and usages of the Jews that they should render to rulers the customary marks of honor, even to prostration on the earth, where these would not be misunderstood.  But Mordecai seem to have felt that he could not, in the present circumstances, render homage to this vile favorite of the king, without degrading his character and his religion before the eyes of the heathen.

entries.title: Esther 3:3
segments: When rulers require their subjects to disobey God, it is the duty of subjects to disobey them; and though this may expose them to the wrath of men, it will meet the approbation of God.

entries.title: Esther 3:4
segments: He had told them that he was a Jew; he seems to have excused himself from bowing before Haman on the ground of his religion as a Jew.

entries.title: Esther 3:6
segments: A man may be so wicked as to regard his own glory more than he does the lives of his fellow men.

entries.title: Esther 3:7
segments:
Cast Pur--the lot; to determine the time when the Jews should be destroyed.  This was done in accordance with the heathenish idea that one day is more lucky than another for the accomplishment of an undertaking. 
 
The lot may be cast into the lap, but the disposal will be of God; and he may so order it as to prevent the end it was intended to subserve.

entries.title: Esther 3:8
segments: To suffer them; suffer them to live.

entries.title: Esther 3:9
segments: The charge of the business; not the business of destroying the Jews, but the pecuniary matters of the king.  Haman offers to pay to the managers of the king's treasury this sum, if the king will grant the decree; intending, no doubt, to collect it out of the spoils of the Jews.  Compare

entries.title: Esther 3:10
segments: Took his ring--and gave it unto Haman; his signet-ring.  Thus he gave him authority to accomplish his wishes.

entries.title: Esther 3:11
segments: The silver is given to thee; by these words the king releases Haman from the condition proposed by him,

. 
 
For the gratification of a worthless favorite, a monarch will sometimes sacrifice the happiness, and even the lives of thousands of his subjects.

entries.title: Esther 3:15
segments:
Shushan was perplexed; on account of the decree to destroy the Jews. 
 
The triumph of the wicked is short; and while Providence for a time seem to favor them, and they glory in their expected success, they may be working out their own destruction.
